for pronouncement this day, the Court pronounced the following:
 ORDER
The instant petition is languishing since 2002 to see its fate and listed under caption 'final hearing list'.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is heard finally.

2. By the instant petition, the petitioner is challenging the order dated 08.12.2000 (Annexure P/7)
passed by the Board of Revenue whereby while setting aside the order dated 31.01.2000 passed by the Sub Divisional Officer and holding that the respondent-company is having bhumiswami right over the land in question by virtue of Section 158 of the M.P. Land Revenue Code, 1959 (for brevity 'Code, 1959'), declared them as bhumiswami directing revenue authorities to correct the record and name of the respondent-company be recorded as bhumiswami of the land in question.
3.

The principal ground of challenging the impugned order passed by the Board of Revenue is that the Board of Revenue exceeded its jurisdiction while making such a declaration and in the given situation, it was incumbent upon the respondent-company to have filed a civil suit and sought for declaration.

4. In contrast, learned counsel for the respondent-company submitted that the respondent-company had moved an application before the Sub Divisional Officer under Section 57 (2) of the Code claiming that since the land was in possession of the respondent- company by virtue of lease-deed granted by the State Government in the year 1943 i.e. before enforcement of the Code of 1959,
therefore, under the provisions of Section 158 of the Code, they acquired the bhumiswami right and as such they sought declaration in that regard.

He submitted that although the Sub Divisional Officer was having jurisdiction to decide such dispute, despite that he refused to entertain the application on the ground that the dispute was not between the State and the company, although it was between the Municipal Corporation and the respondent-company.

He accentuated that the lease-deed was issued by the Municipal Board, therefore, SDO was having no jurisdiction to decide the dispute under Section 57(2) of the Code and that dispute does not fall within the purview of 'dispute', which is to be decided by the authority under Section 57 of the Code.
The order was therefore challenged before the Board of Revenue and in turn, the Board of Revenue came to pass the order and made declaration in favour of the respondent-company.

5. The core question for adjudication involved in the case is as to whether the Board of Revenue was having jurisdiction to make declaration in favour of the respondent-company declaring them to be bhumiswami by virtue of right acquired by them under Section 158 of the Code.

6. To unravel the complexity of the dispute, the adumbration of succinct facts is required, which is as follows :-
The land which is involved in this case occupied by the respondent-Company claiming themselves to be occupant on 02.10.1959 when the Code, 1959 came into force.

The respondent-company acquired the land from the-then Bhopal State and therefore according to respondent No.1, he was an occupant, became bhumiswami on Municipal Corp., Bhopal vs Bhopal Glue & Chemicals Ltd. & Ors.

2 02.10.1959 when Code, 1959 came into force.

As per respondent No.1, they have been in possession and occupying the land since 1943 and that when there was no industry in the Bhopal State, the Nawab of Bhopal and his Industries Department persuaded industrialists to establish industries in Bhopal with a promise of free land and other incentives and thereafter number of industries established by the Industrial Houses from other part of the India and those industries, according to respondent No.1, are now enjoying all the ownership rights.
The respondent's industry is also established in 1943.

In the erstwhile princely state of Bhopal, all lands were owned by the ruler and vacant land situated within the municipal area of Bhopal city also belonged to State and was under the management of the-then Municipal Board.
The said Board was also given the job of Nazul, as there was no Nazul set-up as was existed in the Central Province of British India.
The said arrangement was continued in Bhopal State till it became a Part-C State and then was governed by the Chief Commissioner appointed by the Government of India.
The Government of Bhopal being the owner gave orders awarding land for various performers laying down the terms therefor and it was Municipal Board's job to carry out the orders.

In May, 1943 one Mr Dost Mohd.
travelled from Kanpur and waited on Nawab of Bhopal and his Secretaries and requested that free land exempted from State Custom Duty and City Octori Duty and Water from local water words be given to him.
By an order dated 25.07.1943, the Secretary, Commerce & Industries gave direction to the municipality for finding out the quantum of land required by Mr Dost Mohd.
The letter is available on record as Annexure-R/2.
As per the khasra entries of respective year 1943 (Annexure-R/3), the entire land (disputed land) was the property of the-then Government of Bhopal.
In pursuance to the request made by Mr Dost Mohd, predecessor of respondent was granted land vide order dated 22.09.1943 issued by the Government of Bhopal free of cost with other benefits.
The order dated 22.09.1943 is Annexure-R/4.
A subsequent order containing same date i.e. 22.09.1943 (Annexure-R/5) issued by the Government of Bhopal showing allotment of plot admeasuring 5.8 acre.

The agreement was executed on 10.11.1943 (Annexure-R/6) between then Minister of Commerce &
Industries and M/s. Mehboob Ahmad and Ifthikar Ahmad, two sons of Mr Dost Mohd.
On 01.08.1949 Mr Mehboob Ahmad withdrew from the venture and Mr Ifthikar Ahmad became sole owner of firm and private company known as Bhopal Glues & Chemicals Ltd.
Bhopal State became the Chief Commissioner Province.
Respondent No.1 on 17.09.1954 made an application to the Secretaries of Commerce & Industries Department of Government of Bhopal asking 8 acre of land for the purpose of 99 years.

sentences.text: The respondent-Company requested the Commerce & Industries Department to allot balance 6.93 acres and further on 29.09.1956 Annexure-R/10 was executed for 6.93 acre of land.

In 1959,
Municipal Board, Bhopal was urgently in need of 2.50 acre of land to build a slaughter house and vide letter No.1046 dated 24.04.1959 (Annexure- R/12) wanted to acquire it.
Since the land did not belong to Municipal Board, the Company was persuaded by the Government appointing Administrator to part with 2.50 acre upon payment of cost.

Cost was later-on assessed by the Land Acquisition Officer and vide agreement dated 22.04.1971 (Annexure-R/13), the land was given to Municipal Board, in lieu of it compensation was paid to the respondent.
A cheque was given by the Municipal Board to the respondent-company towards the amount of compensation.

The State of Bhopal finally merged in the State of Madhya Pradesh and after formation of State, the department of Municipal Board of Bhopal merged in the Municipal Corporation, Bhopal and record relating to land of Municipal Board, Bhopal got transferred to Municipal Corporation, Bhopal.
The Municipal Corporation, Bhopal then again executed a lease-deed in favour of respondent on 02.07.1996 for a period of 99 years of the land measuring 6.88 acre on yearly rent.
By another agreement dated 09.09.1956, 6.93 acre land was also leased out to the respondent for a period of 99 years.

After introducing the Code, 1959, the respondent moved an application under Section 57(2) of Code, 1959 before the Nazul Officer, Bhopal contending that the land comprised in Survey Nos.21205, 21206,
21207, 21675, 21250, 21667 and 21670 having total area 11.31 acre leased out to the company by the erstwhile ruler of princely State of Bhopal in the year 1954 for the period of 99 years and they established Glues Factory over that land and since then the land remained in their possession.
Therefore, as per Section 158(1), they be declared bhumiswami and accordingly the revenue record be corrected entering their name therein.

The application was replied by the petitioner, but they have mainly stated that the record of the land is not with them as it was earlier with Nazul department and lease was also executed by erstwhile Municipal Board and therefore in absence of relevant record, they are not in a position to reply the application, but they have admitted the possession of the respondent over the land in question.
On that basis, the Nazul Officer registered a case bearing Revenue Case No. 7A/1/90-91.

The Nazul Officer, Bhopal vide order order dated 14.09.1992 refused to entertain the application under Section 57(2) of Code, 1959 saying that the lease deed executed by the Municipal Board, Bhopal and as such dispute is not between the State and the respondent, but dispute is between the respondent and Municipal Board and therefore, he has no jurisdiction to entertain the application as the dispute does not fall within the dispute as has been referred under Section 52 of Code, 1959, in which the State should be one of the parties.
The copy of order dated 14.09.1992 is available on record as Annexure-P/4.
The said order was assailed by the respondent by filing a revision before the Board of Revenue and that revision was registered as Revision No.195/PVR/92.

The Board of Revenue vide order dated 04.12.1993 set aside the order of Revenue Officer, remitted the matter to decide it afresh after conducting an enquiry on three issues and those issues were also formulated by the Board of Revenue.
Copy of order of Board of Revenue Annexure-P/5.

Thereafter, Nazul Officer, Bhopal again decided the matter on 12.12.1996 dismissed the case holding that under Section 57(2) of Code, 1959 he has no right to entertain the application because dispute is not against the State.
The order of Nazul Officer was again assailed by filing a revision.
The Board of Revenue vide order dated 10.06.1998 allowed the revision and once again remitted the matter for Municipal Corp., Bhopal vs Bhopal Glue & Chemicals Ltd. & Ors.

revision was again preferred by the respondent before the Board of Revenue and that revision was Revision No.501/PVR/2000,
which was finally decided by the Board of Revenue vide order dated 08.12.2000 (Annexure-P/7).

The Board of Revenue finally dealing with the facts involved in the case allowed the application of respondent and declared them bhumiswami in regard to the land admeasuring 11.31 acre and further directed that the revenue record be corrected and name of respondent be entered as bhumiswami in respect of the said land.
This order is impugned in this petition.

7. As has been discussed hereinabove, the challenge is made basically on the ground that the Board of Revenue had no authority to make any declaration in favour of the respondent-company declaring bhumiswami and instead of doing so, the respondent should have filed a suit seeking declaration.

8. Shri Mahajan, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the order passed by the Sub Divisional Officer rejecting the application under Section 57(2) of the Code, 1959 was just and proper for the reason that the dispute is only against the State claiming right over the land held by a person before enforcement of Code, 1959 can be adjudicated by the said revenue authority.

He submitted that in this case, admittedly lease-deed executed by the Municipal Board, Bhopal and later-on that authority vested in the Municipal Corporation, Bhopal and all lands situated within the Municipal area of Bhopal became the land of Municipal Corporation, Bhopal (petitioner herein) and therefore nothing wrong was committed by the Revenue Officer.

He further submitted that that the Board of Revenue did not have any authority to entertain the application as has been rejected by the SDO and the Board of Revenue did not have jurisdiction to make the declaration of bhumiswami as per Section 158(1) of Code, 1959.
He submitted that the order passed by the Board of Revenue is without jurisdiction and therefore it deserves to be set aside.

To reinforce, learned counsel relied upon the decisions reported in re Abde Ali and Ors. v. State of M.P. and Ors. 2018(4) MPLJ 618;
State of M.P. and others v. Balveer Singh and others 2001(3) MPHT 255 and Municipal Council,
Mandsaur v. State of M.P. and others 1972 JLJ 966.
9.

Combating the submissions made on behalf of the petitioner, Shri Ajay Gupta, learned Senior counsel appearing for respondent No.1, submitted that as per the facts and circumstances of case,
the petition is not maintainable on behalf of the petitioner - Municipal Corporation.

In the return,
even respondent No.1 has raised an objection saying that the land originally belonged to the State Government.

The State Government was a party before the Board of Revenue but they did not challenge the order passed by the Board of Revenue and therefore on behalf of Municipal Corporation, the petition cannot be entertained as they have no locus to challenge the same.

Alternatively, it was also submitted by Shri Gupta that the order passed by the Board of Revenue under the provisions of Section 57(2) of the Code, 1959 and as such, as per the provisions of Section 57(3) of Code, 1959, the person aggrieved for challenging the order passed under subsection (2) of Section 57, may institute a civil suit.

He further submitted that before the Sub Divisional Officer, it was submitted by the Municipal Corporation (petitioner) that under the provisions of Section 57, the Municipal Corp., Bhopal vs Bhopal Glue & Chemicals Ltd. & Ors. on 14 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132199071/

If occasion arises the petitioner-Municipal Corporation will file a civil suit.

Quite apart, he submitted that originally the land was allotted to respondent No.1 by the State of Bhopal and thereafter lease executed in favour of Municipal Board, Bhopal for the reason that Nazul department was not separately established but Nazul work was being looked after and conducted by the Municipal Board, Bhopal and State of Bhopal merged in State of M.P., the Municipal Corporation, Bhopal was formed.

He submitted that the Sub Divisional Officer repeatedly committed mistake in considering the legal issue involved in the case that it was basically a dispute raised by the respondent claiming bhumiswami right over the land which was allotted to them by the State of Bhopal and at the time of enforcement of Code, 1959,
the respondent was in possession of the land and therefore seeking declaration as per the requirement of Section 158(1) of Code, 1959 to be declared bhumiswami.

He submitted that when SDO repeatedly not entertaining the dispute despite clear direction of Board of Revenue, which was the higher authority and having supervisory jurisdiction over the Court of Revenue Officer, nothing wrong has been committed by the Board of Revenue deciding the application and determining the right of respondent over the land in question.

Further, he submitted that this Court is under supervisory jurisdiction, entertaining writ under Article 227 of the Constitution having limited power but High Court cannot act as an appellate court to correct the error apparent on face of record much less than error of law.

He further submitted that merely because wrong decision taken by the inferior court or tribunal, the jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution of the High Court is not therefore attracted when order of Tribunal has exceeded its jurisdiction and decided the dispute disregarding the principle of natural justice, the court can interfere invoking power under Article 227.

To bolster his submissions, he placed reliance on a decision of the Supreme Court in re Mohd.
Yunus v. Mohd. Mustaquim and others (1983) 4 SCC 566.

sentences.text: I have patiently heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the rival parties and keenly perused the record.
11. Indeed, the land originally belonged to the State of Bhopal and was allotted to respondent No.1.

The land was allotted in two parts; initially it was 6.88 acre and later 6.93 acre and as such total land admeasuring 13.81 acre, out of which 2.50 acre was later-on acquired by the Municipal Corporation,
Bhopal for the purpose of establishing a slaughter house for which compensation was determined and then paid to respondent No.1.
As such, respondent No.1 had only 11.31 acre of land.
The lease-deed was thereafter executed by the Municipal Corporation in favour of respondent No.1 as per the instructions and order passed by the State.

An application was moved before the Sub Divisional Officer under Section 57(2) of Code, 1959 by respondent No.1, but that application was rejected vide order dated 14.09.1992 by the Sub Divisional Officer on the ground that the dispute does not fall within the purview of Section 57(2) because dispute is between the Municipal Corporation and respondent No.1 and not between the State and respondent No.1.
However, that order was assailed by respondent No.1 before the Board of Revenue and the Board of Revenue remitted the matter to the SDO vide order dated 04.12.1993.

sentences.text: The Nazul Officer/SDO, Bhopal, after remand, decided the case again vide order dated 12.12.1996 and dismissed the application again sticking to his earlier view.
The revision was preferred again before the Board of Revenue, which was allowed vide order dated 10.06.1998 and the matter was once again remitted to SDO, Bhopal for fresh consideration.

Unwaveringly, the Sub Divisional Officer vide order dated 31.01.2000 again rejected the application reiterating same view that the dispute does not fall within the purview of Section 57 (2) of Code, 1959.

Consequentially, the Board of Revenue in revision then decided to deal with the issue and finally vide order dated 08.12.2000 took a view that the respondent-company can be declared bhumiswami and as such revenue entries be corrected recording the name of respondent No.1 as bhumiswami.

13. On the backdrop of preliminary objection raised by the learned senior counsel for respondent No.1 about the maintainability of the petition, I find that as per the admitted position existed in this case and also dealt with by the revenue authority, the land was allotted to the respondent-Company by the State of Bhopal initially in the year 1943 and admittedly since then the Company is in possession of the land and after vesting the State of Bhopal in the State of Madhya Pradesh,
management of land was given to Municipal Corporation, Bhopal and as per the order of State Government, the Municipal Corporation executed the lease of 99 years in favour of respondent-Company.
The Municipal Corporation has also admitted this position before the Sub Divisional Officer and also before the Board of Revenue that record relating to the land is not available with them.

Even on earlier occasion when the SDO passed an order on 31.01.2000 (Annexure-P/6) initially the Corporation did not appear before the revenue authority but the revenue authority again issued notice, then counsel for Municipal Corporation appeared although neither any submission was made nor have they filed any document in their support.

The Sub Divisional Officer in order dated 31.01.2000 (Annexure-P/6) has also observed that the Corporation has assured that after granting land for slaughter house, the remaining land would remain with the respondent-Company and would never be acquired by the Corporation.
The respmdemt-company agreed to it and accepted the compensation for 2.50 acre of land acquired by the Municipal Corporation.

The finding given by the Sub Divisional Officer that indubitably it is found proved that the-then Municipal Board executed the lease as per the direction of the-then State of Bhopal and possession was handed over to the respondent-Company and till then Company is in possession of the land.
However, that order has never been assailed by the Municipal Corporation in which they have also admitted that if occasion arises, they will file civil suit to seek declaration in their favour.
The State has also not assailed the said observation and finding of the Sub Divisional Officer.

The order passed by the Board of Revenue granting declaration under Section 57(2) of Code, 1959 holding that the State is party in the litigation and jurisdiction is well within the revenue authority and also observed that the land originally and basically belonged to the State, but State has not challenged that order and accepted it, therefore, the Municipal Corporation under the existing fact-situation cannot file this writ petition.

Quite apart, I also find that the writ petition is otherwise not maintainable for the reason that the Municipal Corporation has no locus standi to challenge the order passed by the Board of Revenue in relation to the land originally belonged to the State and the State was party to litigation, accepted the said order and did not challenge it further.

14. To crystallize the view, I deem it apposite to quote the provisions of Section 57 of the Code, 1959,
which read as under:-

quarries, minerals and forests reserved or not, and all rights in the sub-soil of any land are the property of the State Government:
Provided that nothing in this section shall, save as otherwise provided in this Code,
be deemed to affect any rights of any person subsisting at the coming into force of this Code in any such property.

sentences.text: (2) Where a dispute arises between the State Government and any person in respect of any right under sub-section (1) such dispute shall be decided by the (Sub-divisional Officer).
(3) Any person aggrieved by any order passed under sub-section (2) may institute a civil suit to contest the validity of the order within a period of one year from the date of such order.
(4) Where a civil suit has been instituted under sub- section (3) against any order such order shall not be subject to appeal or revision."

A bare look to the above-quoted provisions, it emerges that the Board of Revenue has made declaration under the provisions of Section 57(2) and therefore that order cannot be assailed further by filing writ petition, but can be assailed by filing a civil suit under the provisions of subsection (3)
of Section 57.
Ergo, if the petitioner-Municipal Corporation is at all aggrieved with the order of Board of Revenue, it can be assailed by filing a civil suit.

It is also clear from the aforesaid provisions that the order passed by the Sub Divisional Officer can be assailed by availing the remedy of appeal and revision in the higher authority of revenue, but once the revenue authority has passed the order under subsection (2) of Section 57, it cannot be assailed further by availing any other remedy except Municipal Corp., Bhopal vs Bhopal Glue & Chemicals Ltd. & Ors. on 14 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132199071/
8 the remedy of civil suit.

sentences.text: 15. In view of above discourse, firmly I am of the opinion that the writ petition is not maintainable and deserves to be dismissed on two counts as have been discussed in preceding paragraphs.

Before parting with the case, it is worthwhile to mention here that since the writ petition is dismissed on the ground of its maintainability as per the preliminary objection raised by the counsel for the respondent- Company, therefore, there arises no occasion for this Court to enter into other aspects of the matter or deal with the same.
16. Ex consequentia, the writ petition is dismissed being not maintainable.
